title: Vertical Asymptotes and One-Sided Infinite Limits
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find the vertical asymptotes of f(x) = 2x / (x^2 - 4) and analyze one-sided limits around x = 2.
finalAnswer: \text{Vertical asymptotes at } x = 2 \text{ and } x = -2; \quad \lim_{x \to 2^+} f(x) = +\infty, \; \lim_{x \to 2^-} f(x) = -\infty

steps.title: Factor Denominator and Find Singular Points
steps.explanation: Set the simplified denominator to zero to locate candidate vertical asymptotes.
steps.why: A rational function in lowest terms has vertical asymptotes at the zeroes of its denominator.

steps.title: Analyze One-Sided Limit as x -> 2^+
steps.explanation: As x approaches 2 from the right, the numerator is positive and the denominator is small and positive.
steps.why: A positive finite numerator divided by a positive infinitesimal yields +oo.

steps.title: Analyze One-Sided Limit as x -> 2^-
steps.explanation: As x approaches 2 from the left, x - 2 is negative, making the denominator small and negative.
steps.why: A positive finite numerator divided by a negative infinitesimal yields -oo.
